title: Use O(1) removal when draining GraphQL selection lists in the query-cost scanner
answers: why does GraphQL query scanning get slow on wide queries
DoS via large GraphQL selection sets before limit check
body:
Convention (reviewer-enforced): In mlflow/server/graphql/graphql_no_batching.py, do not drain selection lists with list.pop(0) or del lst[0]; each removal shifts all remaining items, making traversal quadratic. Use collections.deque with popleft(), or pop() from a stack when ordering does not matter.
Why it matters here: _MAX_SELECTIONS is checked only after the helper returns, so an oversized selection set forces all of its traversal work before rejection.
Enforcement: _collect_fields_and_aliases builds selections_to_process as a deque and uses popleft(); the main scan loop uses stack.pop().
applies: Applies to any traversal code added to the GraphQL query-cost scanner; the scanner is the only place this rule is established.
says: The server hangs or responds very slowly when validating queries with many fields.
Large queries with extensive field selections take excessive time before being rejected.
Analyzing query complexity for requests with wide selection sets causes severe server lag.
Prevent complex query inspection from slowing down the server on oversized requests.

Applies to any traversal code added to the GraphQL query-cost scanner, such as _collect_fields_and_aliases using selections_to_process. Because _MAX_SELECTIONS is checked only after the helper returns, avoiding quadratic item-shifting prevents large selection sets from exhausting server resources prior to rejection.
